Unlike global fitting methods that may produce excessive small Gaussians in high-density regions, this method estimates models locally, allowing for efficient pre-classified volume ray-casting [S1, unofficial].

The claim is fully supported by the evidence in Source [S1]. The text explicitly states that 'Global GMM fitting... produces multiple small Gaussians in high density regions' (Figure 3 caption) and contrasts this with the proposed method which 'guides local feature classification... as opposed to global fitting'. Furthermore, the text explains that applying a class model with a 'large set of Gaussians' slows down rendering, and this is 'alleviated by using pre-classified volume ray-casting... i.e., each voxel is assigned class memberships during class construction.' Thus, the method estimates models locally (to avoid the issues of global fitting) and uses pre-classified volume ray-casting for efficiency.
